title: A write error on the output file skips the catch: the .partial file stays and the process dies on an unhandled rejection
claim: writeBackup promises (docstring, lines 116-122) that the partial file is deleted on any failure. That only holds when a failure is thrown inside the awaited chain. A failure of the output stream itself is not. failurePromise(out) is a rejecting promise that nothing observes while entries stream: writeChunk races it only on backpressure of the 46-byte header and again for the tag. writeEntryFile (lines 182-190) waits only for the source file's 'end' and never races `failed`. When `out` errors (disk full, removable drive unplugged), the pipe unpipes the cipher, the rejection is unhandled and Node aborts the process. The catch at line 169 never runs, so `await rm(...partial)` never executes. The only test (backup-format.test.ts:179) covers a vanished source file, not a failing destination.
failure_scenario: `pnpm backup --out E:\` (the docs suggest a USB drive) and E: fills up or is unplugged mid-write. Reproduced with fs.createWriteStream patched to raise ENOSPC after 200 KB: the process exits with code 1 through triggerUncaughtException (a stack trace, no 'Backup failed' message) and `x.enc.partial` stays in the output directory (readdir showed ['src','x.enc.partial']). On a full disk the leftover file keeps the space occupied, and every retry can leave another one.
suggested_fix: Make the output stream's error part of the awaited chain: `out.once('error', (e) => { for (const s of [framing, gzip, cipher]) s.destroy(e); })`, and race `failed` (plus outFailed) in writeEntryFile's file-read promise. Alternatively build the write path with stream/promises pipeline(framing, gzip, cipher, sink) and keep the try/catch around it. Add a test with a destination that errors mid-stream.

title: Expected failures (wrong passphrase, damaged file, non-empty destination) crash with a raw Node stack trace
claim: readBackup deliberately throws coded BackupFormatError values (NOT_A_BACKUP, WRONG_PASSPHRASE_OR_DAMAGED, CORRUPT) so that callers can print a friendly message, but neither call site (line 321 in --extract mode, line 361 in the rehearsal) nor main() catches them. `await main()` rejects at the top level. A wrong passphrase is the most likely failure of a tool the owner runs rarely and after a disaster.
failure_scenario: `ANASAQ_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE=wrong node scripts/restore-check.mjs x.enc --extract <dir>` printed `file:///C:/.../backup-format.mjs:84 ... BackupFormatError: Decryption failed: wrong passphrase or damaged file. at Gunzip.<anonymous> ... Node.js v24.19.0` (a source excerpt plus stack, no readable summary). In rehearsal mode the same happens after `supabase stop` and `supabase init` have already run and the exit cleanup runs another `supabase stop`. Missing file, non-empty destination directory and a truncated file end the same way.
suggested_fix: Wrap the body of main() (or the two readBackup calls) in try/catch. For BackupFormatError, print `error.message` to stderr and set exitCode = 1. Optionally run the decrypt before `supabase stop`/`supabase init` so a wrong passphrase costs no CLI calls.

title: Argument loop treats --help/-h and unknown flags as the backup file; a missing --extract value silently starts a full rehearsal
claim: The first argument that is not `--extract` becomes the backup file, so the help branch (`args[i] === '--help' || '-h'`) is only reachable as a second positional and `--help` never prints usage. The check on line 50 (`!backupFile || extractArg === ''`) also lets `--extract` as the last argument through with extractArg undefined, so the script falls back to the full Docker rehearsal instead of refusing. backup.mjs has the same hole at line 41: `--out` as the last argument leaves outArg undefined, so the file is written to ~/ANASAQ-backups rather than the requested directory.
failure_scenario: `pnpm restore-check --help` prompts for the passphrase, then runs `supabase stop --project-id anasaq-restore-check` and `supabase init`, and only then fails with ENOENT for a file named `--help`. `pnpm restore-check backup.enc --extract` (or `--extract $env:UNSET_VAR` expanding to nothing) starts Docker and a multi-minute rehearsal instead of extracting. `pnpm backup --out $env:USB` with an empty variable writes the backup to the home directory while the owner believes it went to the USB drive.
suggested_fix: Handle `--help`/`-h` before positional assignment, reject any other argument starting with `-`, and treat a missing value (args[++i] undefined or starting with `-`) as usage(2), in restore-check.mjs and backup.mjs.

title: --extract writes the plaintext dumps with default permissions (directory 0755, files 0644) on POSIX
claim: S17.4 and G1.4 keep the plaintext out of the repository, and the code comments treat it as highly sensitive (auth password hashes, TOTP secrets, customer records). readBackup itself creates the destination and every file with Node's defaults: mkdir with mode 0o777 and createWriteStream with 0o666, both reduced only by the umask. The default rehearsal is protected because mkdtempSync makes a 0700 parent, but `--extract <dir>` uses a user-chosen directory created by these calls. The docs list macOS/brew as a supported platform.
failure_scenario: On a shared Mac or Linux machine, `pnpm restore-check backup.enc --extract ~/restore` leaves ~/restore (0755) with data.sql and roles.sql (0644). Another local account reads the auth password hashes, TOTP secrets and customer records until the owner deletes the directory. On Windows the user-profile ACL protects it, so the exposure is only on multi-user POSIX hosts.
suggested_fix: Create the destination with `mkdir(destDir, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })` (line 219, also line 382 for sub-directories) and open entry files with `createWriteStream(dest, { mode: 0o600 })` (line 383).

verdict: split (verify first; fix only if real)
title: The Edge Function entrypoints are never linted or type-checked by lint, typecheck, tests or CI
claim: `supabase/functions/**` is ignored by ESLint (this line) and excluded by tsconfig.json line 51. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` has no Deno step. I grepped `src/`, `tests/` and `scripts/` for imports of `functions/*/index`, and there are none, so nothing pulls the six entrypoints into the tsc program. The shared modules are covered only through their importers. `supabase/functions/staff-admin/index.ts` (126 lines) is the owner step-up and role-change endpoint; five other wrappers are 5 lines each. They compile only when `supabase functions serve` or a deploy runs them, and `test:db`/e2e are not run in CI.
failure_scenario: A wrong property name, a missing import or a type error in `staff-admin/index.ts` passes `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` and the whole CI job (all green). It surfaces only as a 500 or a boot failure in a local integration run, or after deploy.
suggested_fix: Add a CI step running `deno check supabase/functions/*/index.ts` (setup-deno, using each function's deno.json import map), or a Deno-typed tsc project for that folder.

title: ACCEPTANCE_PACKAGE=DESIGN-B is rejected, so the DESIGN-B visual evidence can no longer be written
claim: The S21.1 fix routes every spec's screenshots through shotsDir(pkg), which returns the tracked folder only when ACCEPTANCE_PACKAGE === pkg. visual.spec.ts:27 calls shotsDir('DESIGN-B'), and its header comment promises the tracked folder for an ACCEPTANCE_PACKAGE=DESIGN-B run. The unchanged guard in playwright.config.ts only accepts P\d\d or LETTERS-DIGITS. 'DESIGN-B' matches neither (checked: the regex returns false; 'CLEANUP-1' returns true). The run therefore throws before any test starts. Before the fix, visual.spec.ts wrote to artifacts/acceptance/DESIGN-B/screenshots unconditionally. Now the only way to refresh the accepted design evidence is impossible, and the docs (docs/development.md:299) name DESIGN-B as a supported package.
failure_scenario: An orchestrator runs `ACCEPTANCE_PACKAGE=DESIGN-B pnpm test:e2e` to refresh the 50 visual screenshots. Playwright throws 'ACCEPTANCE_PACKAGE must look like P06 or CLEANUP-1, got "DESIGN-B"'. Running without the variable sends the shots to test-results/screenshots/DESIGN-B, so artifacts/acceptance/DESIGN-B/screenshots can never be regenerated.
suggested_fix: Widen the regex to accept DESIGN-B, for example /^(P\d{2}|[A-Z]+-(\d+|[A-Z]))$/ or /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(-[A-Z0-9]+)?$/. Update the error text to match.

title: A complete full run still rewrites both manifests without four committed image entries that no generator produces
claim: The S18.3 fix only stops the rewrite when some source file is missing. The root cause is that a full run builds imageManifest = {} (line 403) and overwrites the committed manifest, so any committed entry the script does not generate is dropped. public/images/manifest.json holds started-street-4, started-mothers-hands, started-child-door and started-closed-door, with their webp files in public/images/started/. Neither IMAGES nor POSTER_ONLY mentions them (grep finds nothing in the script), and the P01 commit 70be5c9 introduced them. The new consent instruction at lines 156-162 tells the owner to 'rerun this script', which is exactly the full run. tests/e2e/cms.spec.ts:22 uses `started-street-4` as the scene image, and src/admin/fields.ts imageIdSchema only accepts ids that are in this manifest.
failure_scenario: After guardian consent, the owner re-adds the five reels to VIDEOS and runs `node scripts/prepare-media.mjs` with every source present. The guard passes, the manifest is rewritten without the four started-* entries, and cms.spec.ts's scene test fails with 'معرّف صورة غير معروف' for started-street-4. The webp files stay orphaned in public/.
suggested_fix: Seed imageManifest from the existing manifest file (as --only and --posters-only do) and overwrite only the generated keys, or add the four entries to IMAGES/POSTER_ONLY with their sources.

title: check:export has no check that guardian-pending films are absent, though the status record says it does
claim: PLANS/EXECUTION-STATUS.md:296 reports 'check:export (51 required files, no secret, no child-film file)'. The script has no such check. The zero-match scan of out/ for '-kid-' was a manual step in AUDIT-1's commands.txt. The only automated guard is a unit test that greps the fixture JSON. If a `-kid-` entry is added back to VIDEOS in prepare-media.mjs (the comment says how) before consent, the manifests, public/ files and the export would carry the films and every gate would pass.
quote: * - no file contains a server-side secret. The patterns match secret values,
failure_scenario: During P11 someone restores the five 4x-kid films to prepare-media.mjs to test the reels and runs pnpm build. check:export reports OK because it looks only for secrets, required files and the demo word, and the export ships them.
suggested_fix: Add a check in check-export.mjs that fails when any file name or text under out/ contains `-kid-` (or a small denylist read from prepare-media.mjs's comment block), and correct the status text to match what the script really checks.

verdict: split (verify first; fix only if real)
title: Extensionless import in vitest.config.ts triggers Vite's native-loader deprecation warning
claim: `pnpm test` prints: 'Your Vite config uses features that are unsupported by configLoader: native ... import ./src/lib/env without a file extension (vitest.config.ts:3:41)'. Vite plans to make the native loader the default in a future major. src/lib/env.ts already uses explicit `.ts` specifiers and tsconfig sets allowImportingTsExtensions: true, so only this one import blocks the switch. The config also carries the `assertLocalTestDatabase()` guard that protects `pnpm test:db` from running against a non-local database.
failure_scenario: A dependency bump moves to the Vite major that defaults to the native config loader. Node then cannot resolve './src/lib/env', vitest.config.ts fails to load, and `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:db` and the CI unit step all exit non-zero before any test runs. Because the config is where the disposable-database guard lives, the failure lands on the safety mechanism.
suggested_fix: Change line 3 to `import { assertLocalTestDatabase } from './src/lib/env.ts'`. The tsconfig already allows it and env.ts already imports with `.ts`.

title: Retention fixture has no coupon redemption, so the purge's third child delete is unproven
claim: finance.buyer_retention_purge() deletes order_items, inventory_reservations and coupon_redemptions before finance.orders (20260930130000_buyer_retention.sql:28-31). coupon_redemptions.order_id is `unique references finance.orders (id)` with no ON DELETE CASCADE (20260927160000_catalog_and_checkout.sql:422), and checkout_expire and checkout_cancel leave that row behind (state 'released') on every coupon order. The fixture at lines 77-90 inserts only an order_items row and an inventory_reservations row. The D42 test therefore proves 2 of the 3 child tables.
quote: // Old enough: an expired hold 91 days ago, with a line and a reservation.
failure_scenario: A buyer uses a coupon and the hold expires. 91 days later the nightly job runs. If the `delete from finance.coupon_redemptions where order_id = any (v_orders)` line is dropped or broken (the function is create or replace), `delete from finance.orders` raises 23503 for that order. The whole purge aborts every night, no order or customer is ever deleted, and pg_cron only logs a failed run. buyer-retention.test.ts stays green because no fixture order has a redemption, so the owner's 90-day retention decision silently stops working.
suggested_fix: Insert a finance.coupon_redemptions row for oldOrder (a fixture coupon, state 'released', old expires_at) and assert it is gone after the purge. Also assert a recent order's redemption survives.

title: X1.1 reset test passes only if policies/store already has a version (hidden demo-catalog dependency)
claim: `approve(APPROVED)` stores store: 1. publishAs computes seq as max(seq)+1 for ('policies','store'). The trigger resets only when the approved value differs from the new seq (audit_fixes.sql:145). Policies are seeded only by scripts/seed-demo-catalog.mjs; scripts/import-content.mjs does not touch them. docs/development.md:130-135 documents db:reset then db:import as the test:db setup and never mentions the demo catalog.
failure_scenario: On a database from `pnpm db:reset` and `pnpm db:import` only, content_versions holds no policies/store, so publishAs returns seq 1. The approved '1' equals the new seq and the trigger correctly does nothing. The test's `expect(after.policy_revisions).toEqual({})` and the audit-row assertions then fail. A correct trigger reads as a failure, and the suite depends on demo-seed state that AUDIT-1's battery happened to have.
suggested_fix: Approve a revision that cannot collide, for example { store: 999, delivery: 999, refund: 999 }, or publish twice and approve the first seq.

title: The 'at the quota nothing is claimed' half never has a priority-0 row pending, so it cannot fail for the intended reason
claim: outbox_claim blocks a row with `(o.priority = 0 or v_sent_today < p_daily_quota - p_reserve) and v_sent_today < p_daily_quota` (audit_fixes.sql:373-374). At the second claim the only pending rows are `mid` (priority 1) and `low` (priority 2). Clause 1 already excludes them at 100 sends, so `claimed` is [] whether or not the hard `v_sent_today < p_daily_quota` clause exists. The priority-0 receipt, the only row that clause governs, was accepted earlier and is no longer pending.
quote: // Fill to exactly the quota: nothing is claimed at all.
failure_scenario: A refactor deletes `and v_sent_today < p_daily_quota`. Receipts (priority 0) are then claimed after 100 sends and Resend answers 429 on each, yet the test stays green.
suggested_fix: Insert a pending priority-0 row before filling to 100 and assert it is not claimed.

title: 'operations sees nothing' became vacuous when S01.1 required visible: true
claim: The fixture publishes `{ cover: ticket }` with no `visible`. Since audit_fixes.sql:49-51 and 79, a post without data->'visible' = true is excluded from media_published_ids(). The media is therefore not public at all, and an operations (authenticated) read returns [] even if a public-read policy were extended to authenticated. The first RLS test (line 218) correctly uses `visible: true`; this one does not.
failure_scenario: Someone changes media_public_read from `to anon` to `to anon, authenticated` so signed-in users can see published images. Operations then reads every published image, but this test still gets [] because its published post is hidden, so the regression goes unnoticed.
suggested_fix: Publish the fixture with visible: true (and assert anon sees the same id) before asserting the operations read is empty.
